name: Computer Use (CodeBridge)
description: Drives the real display through CodeBridge's local daemon, which exposes Computer Use over MCP on a Unix socket. Core does not implement screen capture or accessibility control: it connects to codebridged as a same-user local MCP client and calls computer_start / computer_observe / computer_action / computer_status / computer_stop. Off by default and never started implicitly; the user must enable this entry and authorize the actions in CodeBridge's own approval gate, which Core does not bypass.
auth: Same-user local socket. The daemon classifies a request without a bearer token as local_mcp and authorizes it by peer UID on a 0600 Unix socket, so no credential is configured. The per-launch bearer secret belongs to CodeBridge's tunnel path and is not used here.
cost: No external charge. Every action runs on the user's real display, and CodeBridge's approval policy still decides whether each one may proceed.
requires: CodeBridge.app installed and its daemon codebridged running, with its MCP socket at ~/Library/Application Support/CodeBridge/run/mcp.sock.
verified: 2026-11-01 against the local CodeBridge repository: internal/daemon/ingress.go serves MCP Streamable HTTP (stateless) on a Unix socket only, no TCP listener; a request without a bearer token is CallerLocalMCP; internal/daemon/mcpcomputertools.go registers computer_start, computer_observe, computer_action, computer_status and computer_stop for every caller class, gated by the approval service. Live handshake through this Core's HTTP-over-Unix-socket client against the running daemon: the tool list was returned (computer_start/observe/action/status/stop among 40 tools); no Computer Use session was opened.
limitations: The socket path is the macOS Application Support layout; another OS or a custom -mcp-socket needs this url edited.
computer_start returns approval_required until the human approves in CodeBridge; Core reports that as a tool result and does not retry.
computer_action is limited by CodeBridge's Phase 1 surface (observe and safe pointer movement); Core adds no capability of its own.
